public_rationale: CNBC reported on November 6, 2023 that Cruise said its cars initiated remote-assistance requests roughly every four to five miles before its October 2023 pause. This supports the firm claim that Cruise routinely requested remote assistance (e1). Some requests resolved automatically, and Cruise said human advisors generally supplied wayfinding guidance rather than driving remotely (e1).
limitations: The disclosure does not specify the averaging window or isolate October 2023, the contract’s target period.
Request frequency does not establish how often humans supplied input. The reported assistance figure of “2–4% of the time on average” has no defined denominator.
The packet provides no underlying request logs or independent audit.
The rumor-qualified reference to unnamed other companies is not assessed; their assistance frequency is not established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Cruise, and reportedly others, have been doing remotely-assisted driving in which cars frequently call a remote operations center.

statement.excerpt: Turns out Cruise and (per rumors) others have really been working what we should call “remotely-assisted” driving: the car does *some* of the work, but frequently calls a call-center (aka remote op center).

our_interpretation: Frequent means a routine, recurring part of fleet operations. It does not mean continuous human control.
Use October 2023, the latest completed month before the post, for the recently operating Cruise service described by 'have really been working'.
The firm assertion concerns Cruise. The reference to unnamed others is expressly qualified as rumor.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous operational disclosures establish recurring requests for remote assistance during Cruise's recent driverless operations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Operational records establish that Cruise did not request remote assistance, or did so only exceptionally.

evidence.locator: CEO statement preceding 'How often do remote workers intervene?'
evidence.explanation: Cruise also told CNBC that requests began roughly every four to five miles during the service subsequently paused in October. That supports frequent requests, while its clarification that some requests resolved automatically and advisors supplied guidance limits any inference of frequent remote driving.
